name: American pocket watch
summary: The plain, tough pocket watch that American factories made from 1850 with machine-cut interchangeable parts. It has a white enamel dial with black Arabic numerals and a gold-filled or silver case. The rail grade movement kept time for the railroads.

philosophy.core_thesis: A watch is a public tool. Each part is made to a gauge, the face is clear and the case lasts for decades.
design_principles: Cut each plate and wheel to a gauge, so that a spare part fits any watch of the same model.
Print black Arabic numerals 1 to 12 on a white enamel dial, with a full minute track to 60.
Make the hands as blued spades or plain batons, so that the time shows at a glance.
Adjust a rail grade movement to keep time within 30 seconds a week in five positions.
Fit 21 jewels in a rail grade movement, and set them in gold settings.
Set the hands with a lever beside the crown, so that a knock cannot move them.
Make the case 10 to 14 mm thick, with a screw bezel and a snap back that keep out dust.
Mark the movement with the maker, the grade and a serial number.
anti_patterns: A thin ornamental dress case that bends in a pocket
Script numerals or a crowded dial that slows the eye
Parts filed by hand to fit one watch only
A plastic or steel case of the quartz era
A small dial that cannot be read at arm's length

silhouette.shape: A thick round pocket watch of 16 or 18 size, 43 to 46 mm wide. It has a bow on a pendant and an open-face or hunter case.
silhouette.line: A heavy circle with a deep band, a ring bow and a large crown.
silhouette.fit: The watch rides in a waistcoat pocket on a chain with a fob, and its weight sits low against the body.
silhouette.proportion: Case thickness to width is about 1 to 3.5. The dial fills about 80 per cent of the width. The crown is as wide as the bow.
rules: Keep the numerals large: each numeral is at least 3 mm tall.
Run the minute track to the edge of the dial so that the minute hand can be read exactly.
Put the small seconds dial at 6 o'clock and leave the 12 free.
Make the bow a plain ring that does not turn on the pendant by accident.

fabrics.rule: Use a hard case metal for the shell, fired enamel for the dial and blued steel for the hands, and keep the brass plates inside.

construction.closures: A screw bezel and a snap back keep out dust; a pendant crown winds the watch and a lever beside the crown sets it.
construction.details: An open face or a hunter lid, a bow fixed with a pin and a fob on the chain. The dial or the plate carries a name and a grade.

surface.pattern: Engine-turned or engraved scrolls and a monogram on the case; a plain white dial with black numerals.
surface.gloss: Polished case at 70 to 90 GU; enamel at 80 to 100 GU.
surface.wear: Rub marks wear the gold layer through at the edges and show the brass below; the enamel dial keeps its white.

palette.strategy: Use a white dial and black numerals for legibility, a gold or silver case, and blued hands. Use red only for the 24 hour numerals of a rail dial.

processes: inspection by a rail watch inspector
making.scale: Factory output in model lines: one maker built about 40 million watches, clocks and instruments from 1850 to 1957.
making.signs: A maker's name, a grade and a serial number on the dial and the plate, and a screw bezel on a thick case.

pieces.form: Hunter case with an engraved scroll and monogram
Open-face case with an engine-turned back
Double-sunk white dial with black Arabic numerals
Gilt brass movement plates with damascene
Open-face case with a split-second chronograph

emotion.target_response: A trust in shared time: a clear face, a heavy case and a part that any shop can replace.

use_cases: a prop for a western or a railway drama
a collector guide to antique watches
a vintage object prompt for a pocket watch
avoid_when: the brief wants a thin dress watch

modifiers.how: Thin the case to 8 mm, turn the dial on an engine, blue the hands with open tips, and cut a coin edge.
Shrink the case to 30 mm, add wire lugs and a leather strap, and keep the white dial.
